source.display_title: 05/05/2026 - Eduardo Pérez x Farooq Bey — Lost

prospect.name: Fred
prospect.aka: Joined under the Zoom handle 'f_tal' and then under his wife's account, displayed as 'Michelle Tallner'. Surname is not stated anywhere in the transcript and has NOT been inferred.
prospect.location: North London, England, UK — just north of Alexandra Palace. Swedish, has lived in the UK for 25 years, previously lived in West Hampstead.
prospect.occupation: Handyman — painting, decorating, gardening, renovation, building walls and laying floors, on his feet all day and cycling between jobs. Previously a stockbroker in the City for many years before stepping back.
prospect.family_status: Married; wife trains regularly and is described as toned and fit. Three sons, the eldest 16 and a strong footballer who bench presses around 110 kg and squats 170 kg but 'can't lift a bloody kettlebell'.
prospect.training_background: Has always trained a bit but never seriously; started properly in February. Current week: HIIT with a group of friends on Tuesdays and Thursdays using kettlebells and battle ropes, a 10k run every Wednesday, swimming on Saturdays, and two self-directed half-hour kettlebell sessions on Mondays and Fridays. Discovered kettlebells within the last couple of months and describes himself as a complete novice at them. Previously did calisthenics until he hurt his back, then switched to running. Used to party and drink heavily. Has never worked with a fitness coach, but did work with a professional gun dog trainer over the past year using exactly the film-and-critique model the programme sells.
prospect.medical: No current conditions, injuries or medications disclosed, and none were asked about. Historic back injury from calisthenics that put him out for a period. Takes creatine and protein only, no vitamins. Currently eating roughly 1,300-1,400 calories a day with 170 g of protein and 'literally no carbs' for the past few weeks, alongside six training sessions a week including a 10k run. Names injury as his single biggest risk: 'my biggest risk to reaching my goals, I feel, is injury, and trying too hard.'

signals: Rejected the offer on value rather than capacity, in as many words: 'Oh, it's 100% not worth that to me. I can get that way cheaper than that.'
Self-directed and explicit about it: 'I'm 100% confident I can build myself a program-ish, but I can't tell if I'm doing it right'
Already has a functioning free structure — a HIIT group with friends twice a week, a standing 10k, weekend swims — and is training six days a week without paying anyone
Benchmarks against a cheaper delivery model he has personally validated: a gun dog trainer using film-and-critique, which produced 'very good results'

OVERLAP NOTE: on profile he reads as the_optimizer — already fitter than 95% of his peers by his own estimate, chasing Brad Pitt in Fight Club, a half Ironman and a muscle-up, which is pure good-to-great. Assigned bargain hunter because the defining clause of the_optimizer, that price is a quality signal rather than a barrier, is flatly contradicted at 00:45:15. Same shape as the Hamdi Hmimy call in this batch.

goals.text: Get ripped for this summer — lose body fat over the next couple of months
Be super fit by the time he turns 50, which he has set as a hard deadline
Be able to do a muscle-up
Look like Brad Pitt in Fight Club — a cut, statue-like body he has never had
Learn kettlebells properly and know he is doing them right, as a complete novice
Build strength and flexibility for longevity — 'strength and flexibility is what's going to keep you alive'
Be a role model for his three boys and show the eldest that it can be done at 50
Gain confidence — 'I need confidence... I think it's going to affect everything I do in my life'
Stay fit enough to get through a long physical day's work as a handyman

pains.text: Ten years of saying he would get fit without acting — 'there's always been an excuse... I've started half-hearted'
The injury-then-relapse cycle he fears most — 'you injure yourself, it's game over... then you start eating and drinking again, and it's so easy to get out of step'
Cannot tell whether he is performing kettlebell movements correctly and expects to hurt himself finding out
Wastes time on self-directed sessions — a 30-minute workout takes an hour because he stops to watch ten videos and still does not know what he is doing
Believes his age and dropping hormone levels make muscle gain difficult
Has never had the body he wants despite being sporty and slim, and it is now, in his framing, last chance
Falls into bad habits — historically a heavy drinker who partied a lot
Nutrition has to fit around cooking for a family and be assemblable in fifteen minutes
Eldest son has always struggled to stay fit despite being a good footballer

objections.raw_quote: Oh, it's 100% not worth that to me. I can get that way cheaper than that.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it immediately and closed the call out — 'Well, if that's the case, I'm not going to try and convince you otherwise, right? We're always going to be here, if anything changes, just reach out to us'

objections.raw_quote: That's way out of, well, it's way out of what I would want to spend.
objections.rep_response: Ran the isolating question properly — 'Is it a case of not being able to spend that or you just don't feel like it's worth that?'

objections.raw_quote: I've already decided, mate. It's not a want or... It's happening regardless. You know, I've decided. I've made a decision that I am taking myself to the next level, one way or the other.
objections.rep_response: Tested it with a takeaway — 'you've been doing this routine that you've told me about earlier. It seems to be going well. Just follow that, continue to make progress in that way' — which drew out the kettlebell gap

objections.raw_quote: I'm 100% confident I can build myself a program-ish, but I can't tell if I'm doing it right. I don't want to injure myself... the kettlebells section of it, I'm a complete novice at it.
objections.rep_response: Positioned the film-and-review feedback loop against it well, drawing the parallel to his gun dog trainer, but never addressed that he wants only that one component

objections.raw_quote: my biggest risk to reaching my goals, I feel, is injury, and trying too hard, you know.
objections.rep_response: Not addressed at the time; later covered indirectly by the form-feedback description

evidence: An explicit and immediate no on value: 'That's way out of what I would want to spend' followed by 'Oh, it's 100% not worth that to me. I can get that way cheaper than that.'
The rep accepted it without attempting a rebuttal or a lower tier: 'if that's the case, I'm not going to try and convince you otherwise.'
The call ended within ninety seconds of the price being quoted, with an open-ended 'if anything changes, just reach out' and no follow-up booked.

NOTABLE: the $1,200 one-month trial was not offered here, despite being this rep's standard fallback on a price objection in four other calls in this same batch, and the twelve-month tier was withheld too — 'I don't think you need 12.'

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: intent was extremely high right up to the price. 'I've already decided, mate... It's happening regardless' and 'I get a feeling I'm going to make it happen regardless.' He is going to train either way; the rejection was of this price for this scope, not of the goal.
outcome.next_step: None. Open-ended invitation to email the rep if anything changes; no follow-up booked and no lower-tier product offered or discussed.

notable.note: Third file in this batch titled for a person who does not appear in it. The title names Eduardo Pérez; the man on the call is Fred, a 49-year-old Swede in north London. The rep calls him Fred throughout but slips once mid-pillar and says 'mobility for Eddie should be done the same way we brush our teeth', which suggests he was reading a different name off his own screen while talking to this one. Prospect identity is further obscured because he joined under the handle 'f_tal' and then under his wife's Zoom account, so the display name for most of the call is a woman's. His surname appears nowhere and has not been inferred. On substance: the rep gave the coach roster as 'about 25, 25 clients', having said 30 the previous day and about 60 two days before that — three different figures in three days. He also volunteered specific supplement advice, telling the prospect that vitamin D3 and K2 'just takes your natural testosterone levels to a higher level', and then recommended fasting protocols for over-50s to a man already eating 1,300-1,400 calories a day while training six times a week. The one genuinely excellent moment is the isolating question at 00:45:07, which is the only time in this batch anyone separates cannot-pay from will-not-pay, and it produced the cleanest piece of pricing intelligence in the folder.

quality.notes: Among the worst in the batch, with three compounding defects. First, the entire opening — 00:00:02 to roughly 00:05:00, covering the camera troubleshooting and the initial small talk — is a single unbroken block under the label 'f_tal' containing both speakers' turns with no timestamps. Second, the prospect's label changes mid-call from 'f_tal' to 'Michelle Tallner', which is his wife's account and not a second participant; he flags it himself at 00:05:17 — 'I don't know that that's my wife's name displayed'. Third, ordinary inversion runs throughout: 'Some people don't know how these combos go' at 00:07:50 is labelled Michelle Tallner and is the rep; 'How do you want to show up for her?' at 00:21:00 is labelled Michelle Tallner and is the rep; the whole of the pillar-one delivery alternates labels mid-paragraph. Roles resolved from content throughout. The prospect's surname is genuinely unavailable from this transcript.
